newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

TOP STORIES - The Cabinet has approved Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's bold decision to separate the new administrative court from mainstream courts despite strong opposition from judges. But as a goodwill gesture to disaffected judges, the Cabinet also agreed in principle to upgrade the Judicial Affairs Office to become an independent agency, instead of a department under the Justice Ministry. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The Foreign Ministry has urged Burma to launch an immediate investigation and arrest those responsible for raids carried out last week on three Karen refugee camps in northern Thailand. The Burmese ambassador has been told that although the identity of the aggressors who carried out the Jan 28 and 29 attacks in Tak province was not known, the attacks originated from Burma. (THE NATION)

- A sustainable farming scheme proposed by the Forum of the Poor is to be integrated into the Agriculture Ministry's 1997-2001 action plan. About 40 forum members have told a senior official of the Office of Agricultural Economics that the original plan served the interests of agro-business firms rather than small-scale farmers as it promoted the use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides to produce huge yields for export. (BANGKOK POST) + + + +

- At least 99 billion baht will be trimmed from 1997 government and state enterprise expenditures in an attempt to ease the current account deficit. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has discussed the latest budget cut plans with his three deputies and other senior officials. He is expected to submit the proposal to the Cabinet for approval next week. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Bank of Thailand wants answers from commercial banks that have been putting the squeeze on customers using automated teller machines. Two big banks -- Bangkok Bank and Thai Farmers -- cut two ATM services in mid-January: balance inquiries and withdrawals of less than 500 baht by cardholders using the machines of other banks. Other banks are expected to try similar service cutbacks unless the Bank of Thailand can persuade them to decide otherwise. (BANGKOK POST)

-- The current situation in the petro-chemical industry will not encourage newcomers unless it starts with a large-scale integrated complex comprising a production line which begins upstream and then runs through to the downstream stage, says a senior executive of Siam Cement Plc. He says downstream product manufacturers producing plastic pellets are facing a reduction in profit margins due to the increased prices of raw materials.
